title: NaN sorts above +inf; `max` and `greatest` return NaN
description: NaN is larger than every other value, +inf included: `NaN > inf` is true, `1 < NaN` true; ascending sorts put NaN after +inf (NULLs come first by default); `greatest(1, NaN)` is NaN and `least(1, NaN)` 1; `max` over 1, NaN, -1 is NaN and `min` -1. Quantiles order NaN last: `median(1, NaN, 3)` is 3.0, `percentile_cont(1.0)` NaN.
`SQLOrderingUtil.compareDoubles` orders NaN above everything and -0.0 equal to 0.0.
reference: `GREATEST`: NaN above +inf in sorts, `<`, `MAX`, `greatest` (#89). Spark is native.

evidence.note: positive infinity sorts lower than NaN; NaN goes last in ascending order
`compareDoubles`, `compareFloats`: NaN greatest, the two zeros equal

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `ORDER BY col1` puts NaN after Infinity: -Infinity, 0.0, Infinity, NaN
a `RANGE` frame `1.1 preceding and 'NaN' following` on a `float` column ends at the last row (100.0) for every row: `x + NaN` sorts above every value
ASOF join of NaN with `t.k >= r.k` over r.k in (1.0, NaN) matches NaN: NaN >= NaN and NaN > 1.0 (`spark.sql.join.asofJoin.enabled=true` turns the feature on)

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
